facts.fact: The World Bank's additional-financing paper records 'No' at December 2025 for the establishment of an electronic health record system, a new indicator with targets of Yes by December 2027 or 2028, and describes the EHR as something to be introduced.

The World Bank's results framework gives a baseline of 0 health facilities contracted with the national health insurance scheme holding an electronic health record system at December 2025, against a target of 50 (the results table also shows 60 and 70) by December 2028, out of about 335 contracted facilities; it does not separate primary clinics.

The World Bank paper says that since October 2025 the health ministry (MoH-UHC) has been responsible for the health and insurance systems layer, including the EHR, and that the EHR pilot is supported by the ministry's national health information system division, DSNISI.

The World Bank's additional financing of December 2025 pays for the EHR through performance-based conditions: EUR 866,112.50 on establishment of the system and EUR 173,223 for every 10 contracted facilities with an EHR, with USD 160,000 for equipment and implementation in the centres; no domestic budget line is stated.

The World Bank project paper of December 2025 sets costed, dated targets for the EHR under sub-component 3.1.2 (US$6.50 million for digitalising the insurance scheme): a pilot over a representative sample of primary, secondary and tertiary facilities and laboratories, the system established by 2027-2028 and 50 contracted facilities equipped by December 2028; this is a donor project plan, not a national strategy.

On 24 December 2025 the World Bank put forward additional financing (a EUR 60.6 million credit and US$11 million in grants) that adds new performance-based conditions for establishing an electronic health record system in facilities contracted under the national health insurance scheme, starting with a pilot.
